Related to Next v16 upgrade - Next 16 upgrade is blocked by an update to "@storybook/nextjs". We went in the direction of using vite, since the webpack route was having its own problems.

Removes unnecessary type assertions, and updates tsconfig to solve some issues that were coming up around finding storybook types.

[Issue #8069] Build core workflow state machine logic (#8491)

## Summary
Fixes #8069

## Changes proposed
* Adds a significant amount of core workflow components and utilities to
build upon
* Adds a simple integration with the Python StateMachine library (future
PRs will expand the prototype)
* Adds logic to make one of our SQS events validate and be passed to a
state machine

## Context for reviewers
This change looks far larger than it is, don't be intimidated by the
file count, I put a lot of these components in separate folders, so a
lot of `__init__.py` files were added that heavily inflate the count.
Many of these files contain only a handful of pieces.

The most important piece of code is the event handler. This takes an SQS
event (as a Pydantic object) and does a significant amount of validation
and conversion to make it into a format for our underlying state
machine. This is the core of the whole event processing logic as it has
to:
* Do various validations that the event makes sense (several of these
validations are separated into a workflow service as we will do these
before sending an event as well).
* Fetch entities/users and the workflow itself from the DB.
* Reshape the object into something a bit easier to use now that we've
verified everything (eg. so the state machine won't need to do any
not-null checks)

Effectively, the event handler is mostly a series of guard rails and
error handling, which all is very important, and hopefully very rarely
relevant to the development of the state machines.

The state machine that I have setup is very very barebones, future
tickets will add emails and approval logic to it.

## Validation steps
All contained within the unit tests - no way to directly call it
elsewhere at the moment. see the event handler logic for most of the
core functionality testing.

    <SF424D:RepresentativeTitle>Executive Director</SF424D:RepresentativeTitle>
  </SF424D:AuthorizedRepresentative>

</SF424D:Assurances>

```xml
<SF424D:Assurances xmlns:SF424D="http://apply.grants.gov/forms/SF424D-V1.1" xmlns:att="http://apply.grants.gov/system/Attachments-V1.0" xmlns:globLib="http://app

  <SF424D:AuthorizedRepresentative>
    <SF424D:RepresentativeName>John A. Smith</SF424D:RepresentativeName>
    <SF424D:RepresentativeTitle>Executive Director</SF424D:RepresentativeTitle>
  </SF424D:AuthorizedRepresentative>
  <SF424D:ApplicantOrganizationName>Sample Community Foundation</SF424D:ApplicantOrganizationName>
  <SF424D:SubmittedDate>2026-02-09</SF424D:SubmittedDate>
</SF424D:Assurances>
```

We fixed these namespace issues and all passes XSD checks.

Generated XML from Simpler passes XSD checks.

[Issue #8475] reenable skipped saved opportunity e2e test and fix it (#8481)

Fixes bugs that were causing the "Working saved opportunities page link appears in nav when logged in" e2e test to fail, and re-enables the test

Two things seemed to have been causing this test to fail:

* The expiration time set on the dummy user token that is used in the failing test was too short (5 minutes), and was causing the frontend to try and refresh the token (which failed because the token doesn't exist on the API side)
* The environment file generated for the e2e tests was coming out malformed due to the lack of a newline at the end of the checked in .env.development file. As a result, the necessary env vars for login functionality were not being loaded. This is a regression from commit 534f73201cd. Adding the newline back to the end of the file allows the correct env
vars to come through.
